name: qPCR
description: Quantitative PCR (real-time PCR) for gene expression analysis or DNA quantification. Includes cDNA synthesis setup, plate preparation, and amplification. Adjust primer concentrations and cycling conditions per your assay.
source_note: General educational template for SYBR Green-based qPCR.

steps.title: Prepare cDNA from RNA (if doing RT-qPCR)
steps.description: Synthesize cDNA from total RNA using a reverse transcription kit. Follow manufacturer instructions. Typical input: 0.5–2 µg RNA in a 20 µL reaction. Dilute cDNA 5–10x before use in qPCR.

reagents.name: Reverse transcriptase kit (e.g., SuperScript IV, iScript)

steps.temperature: Per RT kit program (e.g., 25°C 5 min → 50°C 20 min → 85°C 5 min)
steps.notes: Skip this step if starting from gDNA. Dilute cDNA 1:5 to 1:10 in nuclease-free water before qPCR setup.

steps.title: Prepare standard curve dilutions (if needed)
steps.description: Prepare a 10-fold dilution series (e.g., 5 points) from a known quantity of DNA or cDNA standard. These are used to calculate amplification efficiency and absolute quantification.
steps.notes: Typically 1:10 serial dilutions, 5–7 points. Change tips between dilutions.

steps.title: Set up qPCR reactions in plate
steps.description: Prepare the qPCR master mix and dispense into a 96-well (or 384-well) plate. Add samples, standards, and no-template controls (NTC). Each sample should be run in technical triplicates.
steps.notes: Prepare a master mix with all components except template. Dispense master mix first, then add template. Include NTC (no-template control) for each primer pair.
steps.warnings: Protect SYBR Green from prolonged light exposure.

steps.title: Seal and centrifuge plate
steps.description: Seal the plate with an optical adhesive cover. Centrifuge to collect liquid at the bottom and remove air bubbles.
equipment: Plate centrifuge or mini-centrifuge with plate adapter
steps.notes: Ensure no air bubbles remain in wells.

steps.title: Run qPCR program
steps.description: Run the plate on the qPCR instrument. Typical program: initial denaturation (95°C 10 min) → 40 cycles (95°C 15 s / 60°C 60 s) → melt curve (60–95°C ramp).
steps.notes: A melt curve analysis (dissociation curve) at the end verifies single amplicon specificity. Ct values > 35 may indicate non-specific amplification.

steps.title: Data analysis
steps.description: Export Ct values. For relative quantification, use the ΔΔCt method with a reference gene (housekeeping gene). For absolute quantification, use the standard curve.
steps.notes: Check amplification efficiency (90–110% acceptable). Validate reference gene stability.
